# Drawbridge: everything in one file

> Drawbridge is the auth gateway for WSU's container platform at auth.apps.wayne.edu: one OpenID Connect client, signed in through Microsoft Entra ID, in front of every app. It makes sure the visitor signed in, strips every identity header they brought along, and hands the app a short-lived ES256-signed assertion.

The README and the Markdown twin of every page, joined. The index is https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit; do not edit.

---

## README

Source: https://github.com/waynestate/drawbridge/blob/HEAD/README.md

## Drawbridge

**Comes down for signed-in people.**

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub). The container rig has its own script, see "Run the checks".

> The one way into the Citadel. It only comes down for people who signed in.

Drawbridge is the Citadel auth gateway at `auth.apps.wayne.edu`: one OpenID Connect client, signed in through
Microsoft Entra ID, for every app on the platform. It sits in front of the apps as a reverse proxy, makes sure the
visitor has a session, throws away any identity header the visitor tried to bring along, and passes the app either a
short-lived signed assertion that SESAME's `gateway` driver verifies, or plain `X-Authenticated-*` headers for apps
that cannot verify a token yet. Which paths need a login, and which need an Entra authentication context on top, is
declared per app in a config file. Nothing else decides it.

Why a moat and not a lock on each door: every app doing its own OpenID Connect is another chance to get a nonce,
a state check or a token signature wrong. Drawbridge does the sign-in once, in a maintained module
(mod_auth_openidc), and every app only has to check one small signed token.

This repository is published from Wayne State University's internal GitLab and mirrored here. Changes land there
first.

### Where it fits in WELD

WELD is the Wayne State application stack: one contract, several paths that agree, accessibility as a gate, and
decisions written down.

| Part | Job |
|---|---|
| WayneUI | the interface layer (project 0 of the stack) |
| CREED | the shared rules and policy format |
| PROCTOR | checks an app against the version policy |
| Preflight | the shared CI components |
| SESAME | sign-in inside the app; its `gateway` driver verifies what Drawbridge signs |
| HELMET | security headers and CSP reporting |
| Pinstripe | the coding standard presets (Pint, PHPStan, ESLint, Rector) |
| Sourdough | the starter that keeps the stack fed |
| **Drawbridge** | **the one OpenID Connect front door for the Citadel** |

### How it works

```
browser --> Apache httpd (Drawbridge) --> app container
              |  mod_auth_openidc : OpenID Connect client (Entra ID), one session cookie per app host
              |  mod_lua          : strips identity headers on every request, before anything else
              |  mod_rewrite      : asks the PHP signer for an assertion (prg: map)
              |  mod_proxy        : forwards to the app
              `- PHP component    : validates the config, renders the Apache config, signs assertions (ES256)
```

- A request for a **protected** path without a session is redirected to Entra (authorization code flow with PKCE).
  For an **api** path it gets a plain 401, so a script is never handed an HTML login page. A **public** path passes
  through with no identity at all.
- mod_auth_openidc checks the ID token (signature, issuer, audience, nonce, expiry) and keeps the session. The
  claims reach the gateway in the request environment only, never as headers, and no Entra token is passed to an app.
- The assertion is a compact JWT with `typ: drawbridge+jwt` and a `kid`. Claims: `iss` (Drawbridge, never Entra),
  `aud` (the app's host), `sub` (the configured user claim, `accessid` in the example config and `preferred_username`
  if unset), `iat`, `nbf`, `exp`
  (60 seconds by default), `jti`; `auth_time`, `amr` and `acrs` when the ID token carries them; `email`, `name` and
  `affiliations` when configured; and any `extra_claims` (for example `wsuRoles`). A new one is minted for every
  request, and only from an ID token whose `iss` is the configured provider.
- If the signer cannot sign, the answer is 503. A request never reaches the app unsigned.
- Header stripping: the guard removes every inbound `X-Authenticated-*`, `X-Sesame-*`, `X-Drawbridge-*`,
  `OIDC_CLAIM_*`, `OIDC_access_token` (and the module's other token names), `Remote-User`, `X-Forwarded-*`,
  `Forwarded` and similar header, in every hyphen and underscore spelling, on every request, before authentication
  runs. Every header under an owned prefix goes, whatever follows the prefix. It also trims `Connection` to `close`,
  `keep-alive` and `upgrade`, so a client cannot ask the proxy to drop a header the gateway set.

#### Step-up with an authentication context

A path rule can name an Entra authentication context (`c1` to `c99`):

```yaml
protected:
  - /admin/
  - path: /admin/payroll/
    auth_context: c1
```

On that path the gateway asks Entra for the context with the OpenID Connect `claims` request parameter
(`{"id_token":{"acrs":{"essential":true,"value":"c1"}}}`) and lets the request through only when the ID token's
`acrs` array lists `c1`. A visitor already signed in without it is sent back to Entra to step up (mod_auth_openidc
answers with a short page that forwards the browser); an `api` path answers 401. What `c1` actually demands (MFA,
a compliant device, a fresh sign-in) is a Conditional Access policy in Entra, not Drawbridge config. The check is
made twice: by mod_auth_openidc's `Require claim acrs:c1`, and again by the gateway's own stamp step.

#### Signing out

An app links to `/_drawbridge/oidc/callback?logout=`. mod_auth_openidc ends
the gateway session for that host and sends the browser through Entra's sign-out endpoint (named in the provider's
discovery document) back to the address. An address on another host is refused, so the link cannot be used to bounce
visitors elsewhere.

#### Error pages

The errors the gateway answers itself get a small page of their own instead of Apache's default English wall: 403
(an unknown host or a refused path), 502 and 504 (the app is down or taking too long) and 503 (the signer cannot
sign). Each page is one self-contained HTML file under `docker/gateway/errors/`: inline CSS, system fonts, no
scripts, no external assets, dark-mode aware, and no hostname or product name in the text. They are served from
`/_drawbridge/errors/`, which the app hosts keep out of the proxy. Two answers stay deliberately plain: an `api`
path keeps its bare 401, because a script must never be handed an HTML login page, and the `/metrics` endpoint keeps
its empty-body 403 (and 404), because a scrape must not look like a page. The endpoint is not routed by the gateway
config, so these pages cannot reach it; if you wire it up as the Metrics section describes, keep the empty body
inside that location.

#### Response headers

Apps send their own security headers through HELMET, so the gateway never overrides one. On every proxied answer it
adds `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` with `setifempty`, and
an app that sends either keeps its own. When the public scheme is https it also adds
`Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` the same way, with no `includeSubDomains` and no `preload`: the gateway
serves many hosts and must not decide subdomain or preload policy for them.

The pages the gateway answers itself are not behind HELMET and carry their own headers, set plainly because no app
header is expected there. The `/_drawbridge/` locations it owns (the OpenID Connect endpoint on each app host, the
`/up` check on the default host) get `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'`.
The default catch-all host adds `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Cache-Control: no-store` to everything it
answers, including the unknown-host 403 and the error pages.

### Install and quick start

You need Docker. The PHP component needs PHP 8.3 or newer and Composer, but the container carries its own.

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/drawbridge.git; cd drawbridge
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer install --no-interaction
Copy-Item .env.example .env
Copy-Item config\drawbridge.example.yaml config\drawbridge.yaml
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 php bin/drawbridge config:validate --config=config/drawbridge.yaml
docker build -f docker/gateway/Dockerfile -t drawbridge-gateway .
```

**Linux and macOS**

```sh
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/drawbridge.git && cd drawbridge
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer install --no-interaction
cp .env.example .env
cp config/drawbridge.example.yaml config/drawbridge.yaml
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 php bin/drawbridge config:validate --config=config/drawbridge.yaml
docker build -f docker/gateway/Dockerfile -t drawbridge-gateway .
```

With PHP installed locally the same commands are `composer install` and `php bin/drawbridge ...`.

Then run the image with the two files it cannot start without mounted read-only, and the two secrets in its
environment (the entrypoint refuses to start if any is missing, and `render` refuses an unusable secret):

| Item | What it is |
|---|---|
| `drawbridge.yaml` (file) | the per-app config, including the `oidc` block |
| `signing.key` (file) | the ES256 key that signs assertions (`keys:generate` makes one) |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` (env) | the Entra client secret (the variable name is `oidc.client_secret_env`) |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_OIDC_CRYPTO_PASSPHRASE` (env) | mod_auth_openidc's crypto passphrase, at least 32 characters |

```sh
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 --env-file .env \
  -v "$PWD/config/drawbridge.yaml:/etc/drawbridge/drawbridge.yaml:ro" \
  -v "$PWD/secrets:/run/drawbridge:ro" drawbridge-gateway
```

The secrets are never written into the rendered Apache config: it says `OIDCClientSecret "${DRAWBRIDGE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET}"`
and Apache reads the value from its environment. Keys and secrets are never in git. `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` lists where
each real one comes from.

#### Register Drawbridge in Entra ID

One app registration covers every app host. In the Entra admin center, under App registrations:

1. **New registration.** Single tenant. Platform **Web**.
2. **Redirect URIs.** One per app host: `https:///_drawbridge/oidc/callback` (for example
   `https://app1.apps.wayne.edu/_drawbridge/oidc/callback`). Each host gets its own session, so each needs its own
   redirect URI; add one whenever an app is added to the config. Leave the implicit grant boxes unticked: the gateway
   uses the authorization code flow with PKCE.
3. **Certificates & secrets.** Make a client secret and put it in the deployment's secret store as
   `DRAWBRIDGE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`. Note its expiry date: Entra secrets expire, and the gateway cannot sign anyone in
   once it has (see `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`, secret rotation).
4. **Token configuration.** Add the optional ID token claims the config reads: `accessid` (the AccessID, transformed
   from the user principal name with `ExtractMailPrefix`; this is what the example config uses for `oidc.user_claim`),
   `email`, `auth_time`, and `acrs` if any path uses an authentication context. Add `wsuRoles` as a mapped claim (it
   comes from an on-premises AD attribute) and set `acceptMappedClaims: true` in the app manifest, so no custom
   signing key is needed and the metadata URL stays plain; list it in `oidc.extra_claims`. A tenant that does not
   send `accessid` leaves `oidc.user_claim` at `preferred_username`.
5. **Overview.** Copy the Directory (tenant) ID into `oidc.issuer`
   (`https://login.microsoftonline.com//v2.0`) and the Application (client) ID into `oidc.client_id`.
   Neither is a secret, but neither belongs in this repository either.
6. **Authentication contexts** (only if a path uses `auth_context`): in Conditional Access, create the context
   (`c1` ...), and a policy that targets it with whatever it should demand.

### Getting the image

The pipeline builds the gateway image on every merge request and on the default branch, and publishes it to this
project's GitLab container registry when a tag is pushed. The image is at `/gateway:`
(for example `/gateway:0.2.0`). There is no `latest` tag: pin a release.

```sh
docker pull <this project's registry>/gateway:0.2.0
```

The publish job prints the digest it pushed. Verify the image you pulled against it:

```sh
docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' <this project's registry>/gateway:0.2.0
```

The image carries OCI labels (`org.opencontainers.image.source`, `.revision`, `.version`, `.licenses`) set from the
pipeline's commit; a local `docker build` leaves them empty.

### Configuration

One YAML (or PHP array) file declares the gateway, the OpenID Connect provider and each app.
`config/drawbridge.example.yaml` is annotated.

```yaml
oidc:
  issuer: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0
  client_id: <application-client-id>
  client_secret_env: DRAWBRIDGE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET   # the NAME of the variable, never the secret
  user_claim: accessid                               # the AccessID; preferred_username for a tenant that does not send it
  extra_claims: [wsuRoles]                           # copied into the assertion when present

apps:
  - id: app1
    host: app1.apps.wayne.edu
    upstream: http://app1:8080
    mode: assertion          # or "headers", or "both"
    default: login           # what a path with no rule gets
    public: [/up, /assets/]
    protected: [/admin/, {path: /admin/payroll/, auth_context: c1}]
    api: [/api/]
```

The `oidc` block also takes `metadata_url` (defaults to the issuer's `/.well-known/openid-configuration`),
`attribute_claims` (which claim feeds `email`, `name` and `affiliations`; `null` turns one off) and `amr_map` (Entra
`amr` values to the values SESAME's MFA check reads; the default maps `pwd`, `mfa`, `ngcmfa` as `mfa`, `otp`, `rsa`,
`wia`, and the REFEDS MFA URI). The issuer must be https; plain http is accepted only for a `.test` host, which is what
the local rig uses.

Path rules are exact (`/up`) or prefix (a trailing slash, `/assets/`). There are no wildcards and no regular
expressions. The longest rule wins, and an exact rule beats a prefix of the same length. Query strings are never part
of the match. A path with an encoded slash, a backslash, a semicolon, a control character or bad UTF-8 is treated as
`login` (and the guard answers 400). `/_drawbridge` belongs to the gateway.

### Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DRAWBRIDGE_CONFIG` | `/etc/drawbridge/drawbridge.yaml` | the per-app config file |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_PORT` | `8080` | port Apache listens on (non-root, so above 1024) |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_PUBLIC_SCHEME` | `https` | how browsers reach the gateway; feeds `ServerName`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, the redirect URI |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_PUBLIC_PORT` | empty | public port when it is not the scheme default |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_COOKIE_SECURE` | `true` | Secure session cookie; `false` only for a plain-HTTP local rig |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | empty | comma-separated CIDRs allowed to set `X-Forwarded-For`; empty trusts nobody |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` | none, required | the Entra client secret (or whichever name `oidc.client_secret_env` gives) |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_OIDC_CRYPTO_PASSPHRASE` | none, required | encrypts state cookies and sessions; 32+ characters; changing it signs everyone out |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_SIGNING_KEY_FILE` | `/run/drawbridge/signing.key` | ES256 private key for assertions (mounted) |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_SIGNING_KEY_ID` | `drawbridge-1` | `kid` in each token header; change it when the key changes |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_SESSION_CACHE_ENTRIES` | `1000` | entries in the shared-memory cache: sessions, nonces, provider metadata (minimum 10) |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_RUN_DIR` | `/tmp/drawbridge` | scratch for rendered config, locks and the session cache |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_LOG_LEVEL` | `warn` | Apache log level |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_METRICS_TOKEN` | none | bearer token that may read `/metrics`; empty turns the endpoint off unless an allow list is set |
| `DRAWBRIDGE_METRICS_ALLOW` | none | comma list of client IPs/CIDRs allowed to read `/metrics`; empty trusts no address |

### Commands

Run as `php bin/drawbridge ` (or `vendor/bin/drawbridge` when installed as a dependency).

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `config:validate` | checks the config and prints every problem at once, then the provider settings (never the secret, only whether its variable is set); exit 1 if any |
| `explain  ` | says which rule applies to a request, and which authentication context it needs, and why |
| `render` | checks the two secrets in the environment, then writes `apps.conf` and `policy.lua` for Apache (the entrypoint runs this) |
| `keys:generate` | makes an ES256 key pair; refuses to overwrite a file |
| `signer:map` | the long-running process behind Apache's `prg:` map (not for people) |

### Run the checks

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/drawbridge/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md).

```sh
composer ci          # manifest, unit tests, Pint, PHPStan level 8, composer audit
```

The PHPStan and Pint settings come from Pinstripe, the stack's coding standard: `phpstan.neon` includes the raw
PHP cut, and `pint.json` uses the same `per` preset as Pinstripe's `pint/per.json`. This repository adds only its
own paths, PHP version range and excludes.

In Docker, with no local PHP:

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
```

The unit suite checks the assertion against a mirror of SESAME's `gateway` driver rules
(`tests/Support/SesameContract.php`). To check it against the real driver instead, point `SESAME_PATH`
at a SESAME checkout that has been installed (`composer install` in it) and run the integration suite;
without it the suite skips, so `composer ci` stays green:

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -v "C:\path\to\sesame:/sesame:ro" -e SESAME_PATH=/sesame -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && vendor/bin/phpunit --filter RealSesame"
```

The container rig runs the real gateway image with a mock OpenID Connect provider
([mock-oauth2-server](https://github.com/navikt/mock-oauth2-server), pinned) standing in for Entra, and a tiny echo
app. It covers sign-in, public and protected paths, header spoofing (including forged `OIDC_*` headers), path tricks,
forged callbacks, step-up to an authentication context, signature checks against SESAME's `gateway` driver rules, and
logout. The mock signs in anyone with whatever claims the test types into its form, which is exactly what you want
from a stunt double. Nothing in the rig reaches Entra.

```powershell
rig\run.ps1          # Windows
```

```sh
sh rig/run.sh        # Linux, macOS
```

### Using the assertion in an app

Point SESAME's `gateway` driver at Drawbridge: the same issuer, the app's host as the audience, the signing public
key, and the header `X-Sesame-Assertion`. Apps do not parse the token themselves.

### Metrics

Drawbridge can expose a Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint, off by default. It is on when `DRAWBRIDGE_METRICS_TOKEN`
(a bearer token) or `DRAWBRIDGE_METRICS_ALLOW` (a comma list of client IPs/CIDRs) is set, and a request is served
when it presents the token or comes from an allowed address. A disabled or misconfigured endpoint answers 404 and an
unauthorized request answers 403, so the route is never advertised and never served to a stranger. The client
address is `REMOTE_ADDR` (the real client), never a client-supplied header, so a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` cannot
grant access, and the token is compared in constant time.

Point a web server at `bin/metrics` for the path. In the rendered Apache config a location such as:

```apache
<Location "/metrics">
    SetEnvIf Authorization "(.*)" HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=$1
    ScriptAlias /metrics /opt/drawbridge/bin/metrics
</Location>
```

serves it (the `SetEnvIf` passes the bearer token through; without it only the allow list works).

The endpoint serves only what it can see truthfully:

| Metric | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `drawbridge_build_info{version}` | gauge | the gateway is up, and which version |

The assertion-signing counters (`drawbridge_signing_requests_total`, `drawbridge_assertions_signed_total`,
`drawbridge_assertion_errors_total{reason}`) are kept in the signer for in-process use but are not registered on the
endpoint until a shared store lets it see the signer's counters; a counter that is always zero is not shown. Apache,
not PHP, serves the requests, so request counts by path class are not exposed here either, and public requests and
sign-in failures never reach the PHP side; mod_auth_openidc would need its own status or log scraping to expose
those. Labels carry no identity, claim, or token, and the `reason` label is folded to a fixed set, so it stays
low-cardinality.

The counters live in the signer's memory. The endpoint is a separate, per-request process, so by default (the
`InMemory` adapter) it reports build info only. To share the signer's live counters with the endpoint, pass the same
shared adapter (for example `Prometheus\Storage\APCng`, which needs the APCu extension) to both; without a shared
store, PHP's share-nothing model cannot see across processes.

### Documents

- `BEST_PRACTICES.md`: the short list of rules the gateway holds itself to.
- `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`: what is unanswered, what is missing, what is not built yet.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: what changed.
- `site/`: the front page, a static sheet set for the gatehouse (`site/index.html`; see `site/README.md`).

On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/drawbridge/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

### The name

It is a drawbridge, so it goes up on strangers and down on friends. If you find a header it should have caught,
raise the issue. The moat is only as good as the people who keep reporting where it is shallow.

A-101 Gatehouse · section A-A

## Drawbridge

Comes down for signed-in people.

- **draw·bridge noun, not an acronym**: The one way into the Citadel. It comes down only for people who are signed in, and goes back up for everyone else.

One OpenID Connect client at **auth.apps.wayne.edu**, signed in through Microsoft Entra ID, in front of every app on the platform. It makes sure the visitor has a session, throws away any identity header they tried to bring along, and hands the app a 60-second ES256-signed assertion that SESAME verifies.

[Build the gatehouse](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/#build-title) [Read the section](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/#section-title)

![Drawbridge mark: a cream gatehouse tower on a green tile, its bridge lowered on a gold chain](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/brand/drawbridge-avatar-256.png)

The bridge is down for a signed-in visitor. A forged header would be stripped at the gate, before sign-in runs.

A-201 Longitudinal section

### One request through the gatehouse

Apache httpd with four modules and a small PHP component. Every request takes the same passage, in this order.

1. ### Browser
   Arrives with whatever headers it likes. It may have brought a forgery.
   the approach
2. ### Guard
   Strips every inbound identity header, in every hyphen and underscore spelling, before anything else runs.
   mod_lua
3. ### OpenID Connect client
   One client for every app, signed in through Entra ID, one session per app host. No session: off to Entra to sign in.
   mod_auth_openidc
4. ### Signer
   Mints a fresh ES256 assertion for this request. If it cannot sign, the answer is 503.
   mod_rewrite prg: map + PHP
5. ### App
   Gets the request with one signed header, and verifies it with SESAME's `gateway` driver.
   mod_proxy

login

No session? The browser goes to sign in, then comes back.

api

No session? A plain **401**. A script is never handed an HTML login page.

public

Passes through with no identity at all. Public is a decision, not a default.

signer down

**503**. A request never reaches the app unsigned.

Why a moat and not a lock on every door: each app doing its own OpenID Connect is another chance to get a nonce, a state check or a token signature wrong. Drawbridge signs in once, in a maintained module, and every app checks one small signed token.

A-301 Door schedule

### Which doors need a key

Each app declares its paths in one config file. Nothing else decides. Rules are exact (`/up`) or a prefix (`/assets/`); the longest wins, and exact beats a prefix of the same length. No wildcards, no regular expressions, and the query string never chooses.

**Door schedule for `app1.apps.wayne.edu`, from `config/drawbridge.example.yaml`**

| Door | Path | Rule | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | `/up` | exact | public |
| D2 | `/assets/` | prefix | public |
| D3 | `/admin/` | prefix | login |
| D4 | `/api/` | prefix | api |
| D0 | *anything else* | default | login |

```
$ php bin/drawbridge explain app1.apps.wayne.edu /admin/users
app1 /admin/users => login (matched as /admin/users)
```

This box runs the same matching rules in your browser, written to agree with `explain` for the example config. The output lines are the real command's wording.

A-401 Detail · the assertion

### What crosses the bridge

A compact JWT, minted for every request, good for 60 seconds by default. The key never leaves the signer.

header

```
{
  "alg": "ES256",
  "typ": "drawbridge+jwt",
  "kid": "drawbridge-1"
}
```

claims (sample)

```
{
  "iss": "https://auth.apps.wayne.edu",
  "aud": "app1.apps.wayne.edu",
  "sub": "ab1234",
  "iat": 1798000000, "nbf": 1798000000,
  "exp": 1798000060,
  "jti": "4f1c9a2e7b3d",
  "auth_time": 1797999400,
  "amr": ["pwd", "mfa"],
  "email": "…", "name": "…",
  "affiliations": ["staff"]
}
```

Sent as `X-Sesame-Assertion`. Apps that cannot verify a token yet can take plain `X-Authenticated-*` headers instead (`mode: headers`), or both.

#### Left at the gate

Removed from every request, in every hyphen and underscore spelling, before authentication runs. Then the gateway sets its own.

- ~~X-Authenticated-\*~~
- ~~X-Sesame-\*~~
- ~~X-Drawbridge-\*~~
- ~~Remote-User~~
- ~~X-Remote-User~~
- ~~X-Forwarded-\*~~
- ~~Forwarded~~
- ~~X-Real-IP~~
- ~~X-Auth-Request-\*~~
- ~~OIDC-Claim-\*~~
- ~~Proxy~~

`Connection` is trimmed to `close`, `keep-alive` and `upgrade`, so a client cannot ask the proxy to drop a header the gateway set.

A-501 General notes

### Fourteen rules, each with a test

From `BEST_PRACTICES.md`. The contractor shall not improvise.

1. **Strip first.** Every inbound identity header, every spelling, every request, before authentication.
2. **Fail closed.** No session, no signature, a refused path, a missing key or a bad config means no access.
3. **Public is a decision.** A path with no rule gets `login`. Public paths carry no identity.
4. **Match the normalised path.** Encoded slashes, backslashes, semicolons and bad UTF-8 are treated as protected.
5. **Exact or prefix, nothing clever.** The Apache pattern is built from the literal, never typed by hand.
6. **Sign narrowly and briefly.** ES256, a pinned `typ`, one audience per app, a fresh `jti` each time.
7. **Let the module do OpenID Connect.** Drawbridge writes no OAuth client. Forged callbacks and missing contexts are refused.
8. **One session per app host.** A session cookie carried to another host opens nothing there.
9. **Overwrite forwarded headers.** `X-Forwarded-*` come from the gateway, never the client.
10. **Secrets stay out.** Keys are mounted files; the client secret and passphrase live in the environment. Logs carry a reason code, never a subject or a token.
11. **Do not trust the network.** The app verifies the signature even if only the gateway can reach it.
12. **Run small and boring.** Non-root, port above 1024, state under `/tmp`, logs to stdout.
13. **Bounded dependencies.** No `*`, no `dev-master`; `composer audit` runs in CI.
14. **Add headers, never overwrite.** The gateway's headers ride on proxied answers only where the app sent none, so HELMET's stay.

A-601 Construction sequence

### Build the gatehouse

You need Docker. The PHP component wants PHP 8.3+ and Composer, but the container carries its own, so these steps need nothing else.

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```
PS> git clone https://github.com/waynestate/drawbridge.git drawbridge; cd drawbridge
PS> docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer install --no-interaction
PS> Copy-Item .env.example .env
PS> Copy-Item config\drawbridge.example.yaml config\drawbridge.yaml
PS> docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 php bin/drawbridge config:validate --config=config/drawbridge.yaml
The config is valid: 1 app(s).
OpenID Connect provider: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0
   … client id, secret (set or not, never its value), claims, amr map
 - app1 (app1.apps.wayne.edu): default login, 5 path rule(s), mode assertion, auth context: /admin/payroll/ c1
PS> docker build -f docker/gateway/Dockerfile -t drawbridge-gateway .
```

**Linux and macOS**

```
$ git clone https://github.com/waynestate/drawbridge.git drawbridge && cd drawbridge
$ docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer install --no-interaction
$ cp .env.example .env
$ cp config/drawbridge.example.yaml config/drawbridge.yaml
$ docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 php bin/drawbridge config:validate --config=config/drawbridge.yaml
The config is valid: 1 app(s).
OpenID Connect provider: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0
   … client id, secret (set or not, never its value), claims, amr map
 - app1 (app1.apps.wayne.edu): default login, 5 path rule(s), mode assertion, auth context: /admin/payroll/ c1
$ docker build -f docker/gateway/Dockerfile -t drawbridge-gateway .
```

#### Then raise it

The entrypoint refuses to start without these: two files mounted read-only and two secrets in the environment. None of them is ever in git.

- `drawbridge.yaml` the per-app config
- `signing.key` the ES256 key; `keys:generate` makes one
- `DRAWBRIDGE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` the Entra client secret, from the app registration
- `DRAWBRIDGE_OIDC_CRYPTO_PASSPHRASE` encrypts sessions; 32+ characters

```
$ docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 --env-file .env \
    -v "$PWD/config/drawbridge.yaml:/etc/drawbridge/drawbridge.yaml:ro" \
    -v "$PWD/secrets:/run/drawbridge:ro" drawbridge-gateway
```

#### The drafting kit `php bin/drawbridge <command>`

- **`config:validate`**: checks the config and prints every problem at once
- **`explain <host> <path>`**: says which rule applies, and why
- **`render`**: writes `apps.conf` and `policy.lua` for Apache
- **`keys:generate`**: an ES256 key pair; refuses to overwrite

```
$ composer ci     # manifest, unit tests, Pint, PHPStan level 8, composer audit
PS> rig\run.ps1   # the real image, a mock OpenID Connect provider and an echo app (Windows)
$ sh rig/run.sh   # the same rig on Linux and macOS
```

The rig covers sign-in, public and protected paths, header spoofing (forged `OIDC_*` headers too), path tricks, forged callbacks, step-up to an authentication context, signature checks against SESAME's rules, and logout. Nothing in it reaches Entra.

A-602 Specifications

### Specs for your agent

Your coding agent is the contractor. Hand it a spec: copy one, or run it straight in OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT. Each one says what to build, what it may not touch, and to send a question back before it guesses.

#### Get started with Drawbridge

Clone, validate the example config, ask explain about three doors, and run the rig against a mock provider. Nothing reaches Entra.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent helping a Wayne State University developer stand up Drawbridge on their own machine. Drawbridge is the Citadel auth gateway of WELD, the Wayne State application stack: Apache with mod_auth_openidc in front of every app, one OpenID Connect client for Microsoft Entra ID, a guard that strips every identity header a visitor brings, and a 60-second ES256 assertion that SESAME's gateway driver verifies.

Read first:
- https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, the index of Drawbridge's pages, each one as Markdown. Work from them, not from memory.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: read_project_docs with project drawbridge, and list_stack_rules with chapter auth. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages. How to add it: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt
- The README's Install and quick start, Configuration and Commands sections, and config/drawbridge.example.yaml.

Task:
1. If this folder is not a checkout, clone it with `git clone https://github.com/waynestate/drawbridge.git`. Install with `composer install`, or in the composer:2.10.3 container the README uses if there is no PHP 8.3 here.
2. Copy the example config and the example environment file to their working names, as the README does, then run `php bin/drawbridge config:validate --config=config/drawbridge.yaml`.
3. Run the explain command on three paths of app1 (one public, one protected, one api) and tell me which rule wins each time, and why.
4. Run the container rig: rig\run.ps1 on Windows, sh rig/run.sh on Linux and macOS. It signs in against a mock OpenID Connect provider and never reaches Entra.

Constraints:
- Never put a real tenant id, client id, client secret, crypto passphrase or signing key in a file git tracks. Keys and secrets are never in git.
- Leave the guard and the path rules alone: exact or prefix only, no wildcards, no regular expressions.
- Give separate commands for Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux wherever they differ.
- Ask me before you guess, and before anything talks to a real Entra tenant.

Output: the commands you ran, the three explain answers, the rig result, then your questions.
```

#### Or the spec for the app behind the gate

#### A Laravel app behind Drawbridge

Its door schedule for the gate, and SESAME's gateway driver checking the signed assertion on the way in.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent putting a Laravel app at Wayne State University behind Drawbridge, the Citadel auth gateway of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. Drawbridge signs the visitor in and sends the app a short-lived signed assertion in the X-Sesame-Assertion header. The app checks it with SESAME's gateway driver and never parses the token itself.

Read first:
- https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README's Using the assertion in an app and Configuration sections.
- SESAME's pages, https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt: the gateway driver and its Laravel setup.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: list_stack_rules with the permutation that fits this app (laravel-blade, laravel-blade-vue or laravel-inertia-vue) and chapter auth, and read_project_docs with project sesame. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.
- This app's composer.json, config/, routes/ and .env.example.

Task:
1. Draft this app's entry for Drawbridge's config: id, host, upstream, mode assertion, a default, and the public, protected and api paths the app really has (routes/ tells you).
2. Set up SESAME's gateway driver the way SESAME's docs say: the issuer Drawbridge signs with, this app's host as the audience, Drawbridge's public signing key, the X-Sesame-Assertion header and the trusted proxy ranges, all as placeholders in .env.example.
3. Put the auth.sesame middleware on the routes Drawbridge protects, and make sure the api routes answer 401 instead of redirecting.
4. If a path needs step-up (an Entra authentication context such as c1), mark it in the draft and add sesame.context:c1 to that route. What c1 demands is a Conditional Access policy in Entra, not app code.

Constraints:
- Assertion mode, not plain headers: a Laravel app can verify the token, so it does.
- Never trust X-Authenticated-* or any other identity header in the app. Only the verified assertion counts.
- Keep SESAME's replay guard on. Never commit a key, a secret or a real .env.
- Ask me before you guess the host, the issuer or the proxy ranges, and before you change auth middleware that is already there.

Output: the config entry, the SESAME settings as placeholders, the files you changed, then your questions.
```

#### A raw PHP app behind Drawbridge

The same door schedule, and SESAME's gateway driver built by hand, with the check placed before any output.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent putting a raw PHP app (no framework) at Wayne State University behind Drawbridge, the Citadel auth gateway of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. Drawbridge signs the visitor in and sends the app a short-lived signed assertion in the X-Sesame-Assertion header.

Read first:
- https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README's Using the assertion in an app and Configuration sections.
- SESAME's pages, https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt: the gateway driver and the Raw PHP section.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: list_stack_rules with permutation raw-php (raw-php-vue if the app builds Vue) and chapter auth, and read_project_docs with project sesame. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.
- This app's composer.json, its front controller or entry scripts, and how it signs people in today.

Task:
1. Draft this app's entry for Drawbridge's config: id, host, upstream, a default, and the public, protected and api paths the app really has.
2. Assertion mode is the default. Build SESAME's gateway driver as its Raw PHP section shows (public key, issuer, audience, trusted proxies, and a PSR-16 cache for the replay guard), and sign the user in from the verified assertion.
3. Headers mode is only for an app that cannot verify a token yet. If you think this app is one, say why and ask me before you choose it.
4. Replace the app's own sign-in only on the paths Drawbridge protects, and show me the diff before you apply it.

Constraints:
- A raw PHP app has no framework to lean on: show exactly where the check runs, before any output is sent.
- Never trust an identity header the app did not get from a verified assertion.
- Keep the replay guard on. Never commit a key, a secret or a real .env.
- Give separate commands for Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux wherever they differ.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch anything that deploys.

Output: the config entry, where the check runs and the diff, then your questions.
```

The contractor reads the same sheets you do: [llms.txt](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) lists the pages, [llms-full.txt](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/llms-full.txt) holds them in one file, and this page has a [Markdown twin](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/index.md). Nothing here phones home; the buttons only copy text or open the tool you picked. No spec lowers the bridge for anyone who has not signed in.

A-701 Site plan

### Where the gate stands in WELD

[WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/) is the Wayne State app stack: one contract, several paths that agree. Drawbridge is the wall's one door; the rest of the stack lives inside.

1. Drawbridgesigns the visitor in, once
2. [SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/)its gateway driver verifies the token
3. [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/)sets the security headers
4. [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/)renders the page

#### Key

- **[WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/)** the interface layer
- **[CREED](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/)** the shared rules and policy
- **[PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/)** checks an app against the policy
- **[Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/)** the shared CI components
- **[SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/)** sign-in inside the app
- **[HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/)** security headers and CSP reports
- **[Pinstripe](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/)** the coding standard, pressed
- **[Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/)** the starter that keeps the stack fed
- **[WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/)** every part, already joined
- **[Booster](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/)** keeps an app's PHP current
- **[Rollcall](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/)** every app answers "present"
- **[ADVISOR](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/)** what applies, and what to do next
- **[Squire](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/)** carries the release to Citadel
- **Drawbridge** the one OpenID Connect front door *you are here*

A-801 Revision schedule

### Drawn, not yet built

Release 0.2 moves the chain to OpenID Connect with Entra ID; the gate, the guard, the signer and the rig stay. What waits is listed in `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`, with the safer default the code uses until then.

**Planned revisions**

| Rev | Item | Until then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| next | Shared session store, more than one instance | One instance, sessions in its shared memory; a restart signs everyone out. |
| next | Bearer tokens on API paths | An `api` path without a session gets a plain 401. |
| next | Two signing keys at once, for rotation | One key, one `kid`; rotation is a short coordinated window. |
| next | Identity on public paths, if wanted | Public means no identity, ever. |
| next | Live signer counters on /metrics | The off-by-default endpoint reports build info only; counters stay in the signer. |
